lines.speaker: e
lines.text: A Navy warship filmed something drop into the Pacific.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The Pentagon confirmed the video is real.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: In July 2019, off San Diego, the U.S.S. Omaha's thermal camera locked onto a dark ball.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: It glided. It stopped. Then it sank toward the waves.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: On the tape, a sailor shouts: It splashed! It splashed!

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: That's what the screen shows. Now the sea.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The filmmaker who leaked the clip says a Navy submarine searched the spot.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: It found nothing. No wreckage. No debris.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: He also says the ball was about six feet wide, and that it had flown for about an hour.

lines.speaker: e
lines.text: The Pentagon only said the video was taken by Navy personnel, and passed it to its team for unexplained sightings.
